rationale: The question is whether a cheaper teaching format keeps performance, which is an economic evaluation. Two candidate designs were weighed: an analysis of the historical years with optional attendance, and a concurrent comparison in 2027 with tutorial groups allocated to the formats by timetable block. The historical option is refused because self-selection dominates optional attendance (c3). The concurrent comparison supplies a fair effect; the costing approach follows the retrieved costing record, with tutor time valued in sensitivity analysis (c2), and the effect is framed around similar pass rates (c1).
alternatives: Cost-effectiveness analysis from historical optional attendance (refused: self-selection)
Cost comparison alone (refused: says nothing about performance)
Randomising individual students within tutorial groups (refused: contamination between students in the same group)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for cluster allocation as a guide for reporting the allocation
whyNotMoreComplex: A multi-school comparison or a model with long-term outcomes would need data the school does not have; one year of allocation by timetable answers the dean's question with stated uncertainty.

decision.statement: Run a cost-effectiveness analysis of replacing four of eight faculty sessions with calibrated near-peer sessions, using a concurrent comparison of 2027 tutorial groups allocated by timetable block and the school perspective, with tutor time valued in sensitivity analysis.
decision.question: Should the school replace half of the faculty-led examination-skills sessions with near-peer sessions?

criteria.text: Near-peer teaching gives similar pass rates to faculty teaching in a randomised comparison, so a cheaper option may be acceptable.
Existing attendance data cannot give a fair effect estimate.
The curriculum committee refuses allocation by timetable block.

gates.requirement: Approval to use de-identified assessment and attendance data
gates.evidence: Education research committee approval ERC-2026-14 dated 2026-09-17, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Access to sessional fees and teaching charges by year
gates.evidence: Finance office confirmation FIN-2026-088 dated 2026-09-12, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Cost comparison of the formats without an effect measure
Keep faculty sessions and add optional near-peer sessions
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates rest on investigator-supplied records.

summary: Economic evaluation with a concurrent comparison; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
